core_derivations.J2_delta_quotient_argument: Gal(k(t1,t2,y1,y2)/k(t1,t2)) = (Z/2)^2 = <sigma1,sigma2> acting on {P1,-P1,P2,-P2} with cycle types id->1^4, sigma1/sigma2->2.1.1 (2 group elements, same cycle type), sigma1*sigma2->2^2. KN-FIND-a8990a Theorem A's Gal(S_3/L)=(Z/2)^2/Delta (Delta=<sigma1 sigma2>) is a QUOTIENT of this group by Delta, corresponding to the fixed field of Delta = the splitting field of the degree-2 T-polynomial S_3(t1,t2,T). The quotient map sends {id,sigma1sigma2} to the trivial coset (T-roots fixed, S_3 splits: Theorem B's c(t1)=c(t2) case) and {sigma1,sigma2} to the nontrivial coset (T-roots swapped, S_3 irreducible: Theorem B's c(t1)!=c(t2) case). Theorem B is therefore a correct, but coarser, statement about a strictly smaller/different Galois object (order 2, not order 4), and does not by itself constrain the finer 4-point cycle type beyond the coset it belongs to. Full write-up in red-team-report.yaml full_j2_derivation.
core_derivations.J2_internal_consistency_check: H-MONO-0b3def's own S6 Frobenius recipe, specialized to chi(e1^2-4e2)=+1 (automatic for any literal ordered pair of distinct field elements t1,t2, since e1^2-4e2=(t1-t2)^2 is always a nonzero square), already predicts identity/sigma_i/sigma1_sigma2 all three occur -- directly contradicting the same document's S5 claim of only two types. This is an internal inconsistency in IDEA-20260830-1a08f9 independent of any external theorem-reading dispute.
core_derivations.J3_exact_algebra: S=(p-t-Z)/2, N=(p+t-Z)/2 (standard point-count identity, also given in HEUR-WREATH-3's own rigorous_support). S(S-1)+N(N-1) and 2SN are both even functions of t (Theorem B's proven O(1/p) cancellation applies to these merged quantities). S(S-1)-N(N-1) = -t*(p-Z-1) is exactly linear and odd in t: this is the non-cancelling term responsible for the identity/sigma1_sigma2 anomaly. Leading order: identity_density ~ 1/8 - t/(4(p-Z)), sigma1_sigma2_density ~ 1/8 + t/(4(p-Z)); deviation-in-SE ~ -0.756*t and +0.756*t respectively (SE_density ~ sqrt((1/8)(7/8))/(p-Z) for an exhaustive (p-Z)^2-scale census). Full write-up and 6-cell numeric comparison in red-team-report.yaml full_j3_derivation.
